conceptZh: 「雨」變成玩具淋雨站，四個內點各滴下一滴水；小機器人的傘翻成小船，載著它漂走。
object: A solid blue 雨 rain station, a miniature mechanical toy robot, and a yellow umbrella that becomes a boat.
morph: The complete glyph remains rigid and correctly formed. Its four interior dot strokes each release one transparent water bead; the umbrella below flips into a floating bowl-shaped boat.
creativeAngle: 從完整字形直接演出下雨：四個內點各滴一滴，讓雨傘意外變小船。笑點發生在字下方，收尾移走道具，保留完整字形。
promptEn: Create an 8-second animated toy miniature scene with a locked frontal camera, warm soft lighting, and a pale cream background. Center one correctly formed Traditional Chinese glyph, 雨, in saturated solid cobalt blue, filling approximately 70% of frame height with generous margins. Use a clean standard printed form with its distinct top horizontal, outer enclosure and right hook, central vertical, and four clearly separated interior dot strokes. The entire glyph stays rigid, centered, readable, and uncropped throughout. Below it, in the lower margin, a tiny mechanical toy robot with visible wheel feet proudly raises a yellow umbrella. From 0.0–1.8 seconds, the robot settles beneath the rain station and gives its umbrella handle a confident little pat. From 1.8–2.6 seconds, each of the four interior dot strokes releases one transparent water bead, while the blue strokes themselves remain intact. The beads briefly hang beneath their respective dots, then fall toward the umbrella. From 2.6–4.3 seconds, the four beads land with soft plips: the umbrella gently flips upward into a bowl, scoops the robot into its center, and becomes an absurd little boat. The robot sits upright, looks at its newly floating wheel feet, then cheerfully paddles with the umbrella handle as a shallow puddle carries it off to the right. Keep this action beneath the glyph. By 4.5 seconds, the boat, beads, and puddle have cleared completely. Hold only the finished blue 雨, motionless and unobstructed, from 4.5–8.0 seconds. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin, saying exactly “雨、雨、下雨”. Place the first 雨 around 0.5 seconds, the second around 1.5 seconds, and 下雨 around 5.3 seconds during the clear glyph hold; pronounce 雨 as ㄩˇ each time. Stop speaking after the word. Use only quiet water plips and a gentle umbrella squeak beneath the voice, with no music. The only on-screen text is the single target glyph 雨; keep the vocabulary audio-only, with no subtitles, additional lettering, watermark, clutter, or flashing effects.

conceptZh: 濕答答的小怪獸甩出四滴水，填成「雨」字的四個內點，自己卻蓬成一顆大毛球。
object: A rain-soaked fuzzy pocket creature toy, its gachapon capsule, and a cobalt-blue glyph with four recessed dot wells.
morph: Four blue droplets shaken from the creature's fur flow into four dot-shaped recesses, completing 雨 while its structural strokes remain fixed.
creativeAngle: 改用扭蛋小怪獸甩乾身體的反差笑點：四滴水補齊字形，原本扁塌的小怪獸卻瞬間蓬成大毛球，驚訝地滾走。固定外框與中豎，讓四個內點的位置清楚可辨。
promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second stylized toy animation with a locked frontal camera, soft warm lighting, and a pale peach background. Center a shallow cobalt-blue relief of the Traditional Chinese character 雨, occupying about 70% of frame height with generous margins. Build it from an accurate standard Traditional Chinese print glyph: preserve the separate top horizontal, outer frame with its right hook, central vertical, and four correctly placed interior dot strokes, two on each side. Initially, the structural strokes are solid blue while the four dot locations are shallow, background-colored recesses. The teaching subject stays centered and uncropped throughout.

The original lead is an impulsive, round fuzzy pocket creature toy with tiny rubber feet, expressive bead eyes, and comically overconfident energy. Its only accessory is a hinged gachapon capsule in the lower margin. At 0.0–0.7 seconds, the capsule pops open softly and the creature bursts out dripping wet, its fur plastered flat. The capsule rocks out of frame. Through 2.0 seconds, the creature makes two rubbery ricochets against the glyph's rigid lower side strokes, trying to bounce itself dry. It lands at the bottom center, still soggy, and gives its drooping fur an incredulous glance. Keep these movements small enough that the glyph's structure remains easy to follow.

At 2.0–2.5 seconds, it plants its feet and winds up for one determined full-body shake. From 2.5–3.7 seconds, exactly four cobalt-blue water droplets fling outward in short, clearly visible arcs: one into each interior dot recess. Each droplet flows into its precise printed dot shape without connecting to neighboring strokes. As the last droplet settles, the now-dry creature's fur suddenly expands into an absurdly oversized round pompom. Its tiny feet no longer reach the floor! It blinks, paddles its feet in the air, then rolls gently out through the lower margin, clearing the composition by 4.7 seconds. The completed glyph never bends or reacts to the impacts. Hold only the fully formed, solid cobalt-blue 雨 completely motionless and unobstructed from 4.7–8.0 seconds.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin, saying exactly “雨、雨、雨水”. Say the first 雨 around 0.5 seconds, the second around 1.6 seconds, and 雨水 around 5.5 seconds during the clear final hold. Pronounce 雨 as ㄩˇ throughout and stop after 雨水. Add restrained rubber boings, four soft water plips, and a gentle fur-puff sound beneath the voice; no music. Use exclusively stylized animated toy forms. The single target glyph 雨 is the only on-screen text; vocabulary remains audio-only, with no subtitles, logos, watermark, clutter, or flashing effects.
